A few studies in making room for good content.

These example projects explore different ways to use the same theme: an editorial journal, a working portfolio, and a resource library. They are design studies, not client commissions.

Selected studies

The Quiet Edit

A journal where long articles, useful metadata, and an open discussion can sit together without competing for attention.

The resource shelf

A short reference library that favors descriptive links and clear sections over an endless grid of cards.

Browse the resources →

Behind the journal

The brief was simple: make the article easy to read, make the next step easy to find, and make publishing feel familiar.

The result uses a narrow text column, wider artwork when it needs room, and the same small set of typography and spacing decisions across the site.

Read the design notes →

Different pages. One visual language.

A portfolio can be wider and more visual than a journal without looking like a different website. Native blocks let each page have its own rhythm while keeping the fundamentals consistent.
